title: Agora Workbench: Co-Located Loopback Sidecar Process Lifecycle, Host/Port Env Lock & Atomic Teardown
summary: Agora Workbench shares heavy global runtime dependencies (such as ML models) across isolated CodeExecutionServer kernel sessions by launching co-located loopback HTTP sidecars via SidecarManager. On start_all(), duplicate names fail early, partial startup failures trigger atomic stop_all() rollback, SIDECAR_HOST and SIDECAR_PORT overwrite caller spec.env overrides so readiness polling targets the configured loopback socket, and stop_all() tears down process groups via SIGTERM before a 10.0s grace timeout escalates to SIGKILL.

references.description: SidecarConfig schema defining command, use_env_python, url_env_var, host=127.0.0.1, port, health_path, and readiness_timeout_s
SidecarManager.start_all and _start_one with duplicate-name rejection, start_new_session=True, atomic rollback, and url_env_var export
_resolve_argv requiring built kernel Python, _build_env locking SIDECAR_HOST/SIDECAR_PORT, and 1.0s health polling loop
Process-group SIGTERM shutdown with _TERMINATION_GRACE_S=10.0 escalation to SIGKILL and env cleanup

author: repo-triad-forge
distilled_learning: Co-located loopback sidecars amortize heavy global state across isolated execution kernels while preventing startup leaks via atomic rollback and reserved SIDECAR_HOST/SIDECAR_PORT env locking.
